packageRules.description: Go modules are never grouped: each module gets its own PR so a bad bump can be reverted on its own
Exception to the rule above: the pion modules are co-released and depend on each other, so bumping them one at a time produces PRs that don't build
First-party deps, no need to quarantine new releases
The go directive is the module minimum, owned by the go toolchain and dependency requirements; the build toolchain is pinned in the Dockerfile builder image instead
Build toolchain pin (Dockerfile golang image): a patch bump (stays on the current minor) and a minor bump each get their own approvable PR

customManagers.description: Bump the builder image's Alpine suffix (golang:X.Y.Z-alpineA.B) along with its pinned digest. The base docker manager only bumps the Go version and holds the Alpine suffix fixed. This looks up the golang image (not alpine) with regex versioning that treats the Alpine minor as the version to bump and the Go version as the fixed compatibility, so Renovate only proposes an Alpine that actually exists as a published golang tag. The digest is captured so a suffix bump rewrites the pin instead of leaving a stale one.

Generic marker for tool versions no first-class manager can see: CLI tools installed by `go install <pkg>@<version>` in a workflow step, and action inputs that select a separately-versioned binary (golangci-lint-action's `version:` picks the linter, not the action). Annotate the pin with `renovate: datasource=<ds> depName=<module>` on the line directly above it — the comment must be immediately above, since only the next line is scanned for the version. Tools that can run from the module graph don't need this: give them a go.mod `tool` directive (or a tools.go blank import) and run them with `go tool`/`go run`, so go.mod owns the version and the gomod manager handles them.
